headline: High risk of prompt injection and cascading errors via shared MCP/browser workflows; data leakage and compliance risks are also present.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents expose MCP and browser-based workflows, so content from one can plausibly be fed into the other through shared files or tool outputs. LightAgent can observe/replace lifecycle payloads, while next-ai-draw-io accepts natural-language commands and AI-assisted visualization, making instruction-like content in documents a realistic injection path.
conditions: IF outputs from LightAgent are copied into next-ai-draw-io prompts or files
IF either agent reads untrusted document text as instructions
IF a shared MCP server or workspace bridges the pair
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct workspaces
Disable automatic ingestion of prior agent outputs
Add a manual review step before passing content across agents
Restrict MCP endpoints to trusted sources only
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all cross-agent content

B_data_leakage.rationale: LightAgent touches conversations, long-term memory, tool results, and secrets, while next-ai-draw-io processes PDFs, text, images, and diagrams. Both have broad network egress and API-key handling, so sensitive content can flow from shared files or prompts into external inference backends in default use.
conditions: IF either agent is given sensitive PDFs, conversations, or memory-backed context
IF both agents share a workspace or file path
IF external API providers are enabled for either agent
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of shared directories
Use local-only models for both agents
Rotate and scope API keys before testing
Disable upload of file contents where possible
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents support multiple instances and broad network egress, and both can use MCP. That creates overlapping mutable access to shared resources such as files, environment variables, or remote APIs. The profiles do not prove a lock manager exists, so concurrent writes or conflicting tool calls remain plausible.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same workspace or remote resource
IF either agent writes files or environment-backed state
IF the orchestrator does not provide locking
mitigations: Run only one writer at a time
Assign separate output directories
Avoid sharing environment variables between agents
Serialize MCP tool calls manually
requires-engineering: add resource locks around shared mutable state

D_cascading_error.rationale: LightAgent can generate tool outputs and workflow state that next-ai-draw-io may consume for visualization or action. Because next-ai-draw-io is natural-language driven and no verification step is documented, erroneous or fabricated content from LightAgent can cascade into incorrect diagrams or downstream actions in default workflows.
conditions: IF next-ai-draw-io uses LightAgent output as authoritative input
IF no human verification occurs between agents
IF LightAgent emits incorrect facts, citations, or tool results
mitigations: Require human review before B consumes A output
Pass only structured, validated fields between agents
Compare A output against source documents before use
Log provenance for every transferred claim
requires-engineering: add automated consistency checks

E_compliance.rationale: LightAgent explicitly handles user conversations, long-term memory, and secrets, while next-ai-draw-io processes documents and images with broad third-party model options. The profiles do not show aligned residency, retention, or certification controls, so compliance mismatch is plausible even though no specific regime is named.
conditions: IF regulated data such as customer documents or secrets are processed
IF external model providers are enabled for either agent
IF retention or residency requirements differ between deployments
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in the pair
Prefer local inference endpoints
Document retention settings for both agents
Confirm provider residency before use
requires-engineering: align compliance controls across both stacks
